title: Geo-fenced analytics routing and compliance DR policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement geo-fenced routing and a compliance-driven disaster-recovery policy for analytics events generated by the Console backend. Goal: ensure tenant analytics are stored and processed only in legally-allowed regions while providing an operational DR path that preserves SLA for dashboards and rollout metrics. This ticket covers the routing layer, topic/stream namespacing, residency tag enforcement, fallbacks for cross-region outages, and service-level monitoring and alerts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Console events for tenants with a region residency tag are always written to a primary region-specific topic/ingest pipeline under normal operation.

2) For configured tenants, a DR replication path to a secondary region exists but is only writable under operator-approved failover or when a tenant has explicitly opted into cross-region replication.
3) Residency enforcement is audited: every write includes a signed residency-check header and is logged to an immutable audit stream.
4) End-to-end latency for regional writes remains within current SLO (+10% tolerance for routing layer overhead).
5) Migration and rollback procedures documented and tested in staging with smoke dashboards and chaos tests.
design_decisions: Use tenant residency metadata attached to tokens/tenant configs as the single source of truth for routing decisions.
Implement routing at the producer side (Console backend service) with a lightweight region-aware client that prefers local region endpoints to minimize cross-region egress.
Replicate via controlled, operator-configurable asynchronous pipelines (Kafka Connect / Mirror + encryption-in-transit). Synchronous cross-region writes are disallowed to avoid tail latency spikes.
Store residency audit events in an append-only, tamper-evident audit topic for compliance export and legal requests.
technical_notes: We will add a region-aware publish client inside console-backend that resolves tenant residency from cache (TTL 30s) and falls back to Control Plane lookup when missing. The client will tag messages with 'residency:eu-west-1' style headers. Kafka topic naming convention: analytics.<region>.<ingest-shard>. Tenants configured for DR will have a separate replication policy object referencing allowed secondary regions. Cross-region replication will be disabled by default for regulated tenants. For DR activation, operators must set a 'dr_state' on tenant config which enables writes to the secondary pipeline and triggers an audit event.
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add residency-aware client to Console behind feature flag and route a small percentage of inert test traffic to regional topics. Phase 2: Backfill existing tenant residency tags via a batch job and enable strict-routing for a pilot set of tenants (internal + low-risk customers). Phase 3: Open opt-in for non-regulated customers and run DR rehearsal with failover to secondary pipeline in staging. Phase 4: Gradual rollout to production with monitoring and on-call runbooks.
rollback_plan: If route client causes errors or latency regressions, flip feature flag to global-fallback mode which writes to the existing global analytics topic. Revoke DR writes by clearing 'dr_state' and replaying committed offsets from the primary regional topic. All rollbacks must be followed by a compliance audit-record confirming no cross-region writes for regulated tenants occurred.
monitoring: Routing decision latency (time to resolve residency + publish)
Cross-region write count and egress bytes by tenant
Audit-topic tamper checks and consumer-lag alerts
DR activation events and operator approvals
cost_considerations: Estimated delta: +12% monthly egress and topic storage for pilot tenants if DR enabled. Operator-managed DR reduces constant costs compared to always-on replication. We'll add a pricing note to Console billing that flags tenants opting into cross-region replication.
tradeoffs: Synchronous enforcement of residency at write time would provide stronger guarantees but would increase tail latency and reduce availability. Chosen approach trades strict immediate global durability for lower latency and operator-controlled failover. There is a residual risk of misconfiguration; mitigated via an immutable audit stream and preflight validation in the control plane.
security_and_compliance: All cross-region replication traffic must use mTLS and customer keys remain in the home region HSM where required. Audit stream retention is 7 years for regulated tenants and access-controlled via RBAC. Security review required prior to phase-3 rollout.
